narrative.overview: This design system serves a practical, event-driven ticketing workflow: public purchase, manual payment verification, e-ticket delivery, and gate check-in. The visual language is deliberately restrained — one dominant blue accent, a calm neutral canvas, and status colors that appear only when an order or gate state demands attention. The system is mobile-first with a single-column flow below 760px, and it uses flat, low-contrast surfaces so that information density and readability always win over decorative flourish. All state colors are contextual by design: green means 'confirmed', red means 'rejected or invalid', amber means 'pending'. No decorative gradient or color wash appears outside the event poster card, which is the system's one sanctioned use of a primary-to-accent gradient to signal 'this is an event'.
keyCharacteristics: Single primary accent (Royal Blue #1d4ed8) with a single secondary accent (Amber #f59e0b)
Flat surfaces; shadows appear only on raised containers (cards, modals, toasts, header)
12px radius as the universal container corner; 999px pill radius for chips and nav items
Status colors (green / red / amber) appear only in their semantic contexts
44px minimum touch-target height on all buttons and inputs
Mobile-first: below 760px, navigation collapses into a stacked full-width list

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Primary blue (--primary) is the only chromatic color that is always present in the UI. Status colors appear only in their semantic contexts — order results, gate-scan results, alerts, and status chips. No decorative gradient or colored fill that does not carry state is permitted, with the sole exception of the event poster placeholder.

rules.name: The Neutral Canvas Rule
rules.body: The background (#f4f6fb) and card (#ffffff) colors are the default surface vocabulary. All content sits on white or the soft canvas. Colored surfaces (status backgrounds, the header, button fills) are reserved for state and interaction.

rules.name: The Runtime Override Rule
rules.body: --primary and --accent are CSS custom properties set via document.documentElement.style.setProperty() from the Settings sheet at boot time (applyTheme() in JavaScript.html). The values in DESIGN.md and Style.html are the defaults; a live deployment may show different hues. All component color references should use var(--primary) and var(--accent) where possible rather than hard-coded hex.

rules.name: The No Display Font Rule
rules.body: The system does not load a custom display face. Hierarchy comes from the system stack and weight/size scaling only. If a decorative header is needed, use the system font at a larger size and heavier weight — not a separate typeface.

rules.name: The Mono-for-IDs Rule
rules.body: Machine-generated identifiers (ticket IDs, order IDs, usernames, QR code text) always use the .mono class. This visually distinguishes user-facing data from prose and supports the gate scan-readback workflow.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: The page canvas is flat. Shadows appear only on raised surfaces (cards, stat cards, modals, toasts, the sticky header). No ambient shadow on the body element. Elevation changes on hover use a deeper blur (0 10px 30px) with the same slate tint; they never change color or add colored halos.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Only Rule
rules.body: The system defines exactly two shadow values: the card shadow and the header shadow. No new shadow layers may be introduced. If a new surface type needs elevation, reuse one of the two existing shadows.

rules.name: The 12px Container Rule
rules.body: 12px is the default radius for all card-like containers. Do not mix radii within a single card; the inner content should follow the outer shape. The toast (14px) and gate result banner (20px) are documented exceptions with distinct roles.

rules.name: The Pill-Only Rule
rules.body: 999px radius is reserved for chips, navigation pills, the progress bar, and the QR code container. No other element uses a pill shape.

dos: Do use var(--primary) and var(--accent) for all interactive color references; the Settings sheet overrides these values at runtime.
Do keep primary blue as the only always-present accent. Status colors are contextual and must not be used for general decoration.
Do use the 44px minimum height for all buttons and input fields to maintain touch accessibility.
Do use 12px as the default radius for cards, buttons, modals, alerts, and ticket cards.
Do use the 999px pill radius only for chips, navigation pills, progress bars, and QR containers.
Do keep the shadow vocabulary to the two defined shadows (card shadow and header shadow). Do not add new shadow layers.
Do use the system font stack; do not load a custom web font.
Do use the .mono class for all machine-generated identifiers (ticket IDs, order IDs, usernames, QR text).
Do keep the single-column mobile layout below 760px.
Do use zebra striping (#f1f5f9 on even rows) for all data tables.
donts: Don't use gradients for general backgrounds or fills. The event poster gradient (linear-gradient(135deg, var(--primary), var(--accent))) is the sole exception.
Don't use status colors (green, red, amber) for buttons or chips outside their semantic contexts (order results, gate scan results, alerts, ticket status).
Don't add hover shadows or elevation changes to the page canvas; the system is flat by default.
Don't use large radii (24px or more) on content cards; 12px is the ceiling for standard container shapes. The gate result banner (20px) and toast (14px) are documented exceptions.
Don't mix multiple accent colors on the same screen; one blue, one amber, and status colors are the full chromatic palette.
Don't use color as the sole indicator of status — always pair status color with text or icon, per accessibility commitment in PRODUCT.md.
